output.review_comment:
Requesting changes. I only had the diff; I couldn't see the tests, docstring or constant values, and the PR has no description.

The period change (1–30 days late = one period) and the half-up rounding look like reasonable spec fixes. The change to how the cap and minimum interact is the problem.

The old code applied the minimum, then the 20% cap, so the fee never went above the cap. The new code returns the cap if the fee is over it, otherwise max(fee, MINIMUM). When the minimum is above the cap (small balances), the result gets worse as the fee grows. Example with a $5 minimum and a $10 balance ($2 cap): a $1.50 fee becomes $5, over the cap, but a $2.50 fee becomes $2. So a customer who is later or owes more can pay less, and the cap and minimum each apply only sometimes. That doesn't read like a finance rule; it looks like branching written to make particular test cases pass.

Please:
1. Add a PR description explaining the spec behind each change, pointing to the tests and docstring.
2. Pick one consistent rule for when the minimum is above the cap: either the cap always wins (old behaviour) or the minimum always wins. If a test really expects results that go up and down like this, raise it with the teammate and finance instead of coding around it.
3. Confirm the round-up and half-up changes match the docstring and aren't just tuned to the test values.
